stem.text: Let f be the function defined by \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{2 x^{2} - 16 x + 30}{x - 3}, & x \ne 3 \\ 3, & x = 3 \end{cases} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = 3 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is not continuous at \( x = 3 \), because the limit of f(x) there is -4 while f(3) = 3.

worked_solution.text: The function value at the boundary is \( f(3) = 3 \), from the second line of the rule.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the function at the input

worked_solution.text: For \( x \ne 3 \) the quotient simplifies to \( 2 x - 10 \), so \( \lim_{x \to 3} f(x) = -4 \) from both sides.
The limit exists and equals -4, but \( f(3) = 3 \), so the limit does not equal the function value and f is not continuous at \( x = 3 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: the limit must equal the function value

options.derivation: x = 3 substituted into the quotient, which applies only for x not equal to 3, giving 0/0

options.label: f is continuous at \( x = 3 \), because the limit of f(x) there is 3, which equals f(3).
